B18C001.summary: Janamejaya asks what heavenly regions his ancestors, the Pandavas and Kauravas, reached. Yudhishthira sees Duryodhana honored in heaven and refuses to share it, but Narada reminds him that enmities end in heaven. Yudhishthira then asks where his fallen brothers and allies are, showing that his grief is not yet settled.

scenes.B18C001S01: Yudhishthira sees Duryodhana seated in glory in heaven, rejects sharing that place, and Narada reminds him that enmities end there.
scenes.B18C001S02: Narada urges Yudhishthira to forget old wrongs and greet Duryodhana properly, and Yudhishthira asks where his fallen kin and allies are.

shots.B18C001S01H01: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Sarasvati.
shots.B18C001S01H02: Janamejaya asks what regions his ancestors reached in heaven, and asks Vaishampayana to tell him.
shots.B18C001S01H03: Yudhishthira sees Duryodhana seated in splendor among the gods and is filled with rage, and turns away.
shots.B18C001S01H04: Yudhishthira tells his companions he will not share heaven with Duryodhana, recalling the wrongs done to his family.
shots.B18C001S01H05: Narada smiles and says enmities end in heaven. He notes Duryodhana's honor there for dying as a warrior.
shots.B18C001S02H01: Narada tells Yudhishthira to put aside the old sufferings and greet Duryodhana as heaven's customs require.
shots.B18C001S02H02: Yudhishthira asks where his brothers and allies are, and names a long list of fallen heroes he does not see.

B18C002.summary: Yudhishthira says heaven means nothing without his brothers and allies, and the messenger leads him down a foul, hellish road. Pleading voices from the suffering halt him, and when he asks who they are, they answer with the names of his dead kin, Karna, the Pandavas and Draupadi. Yudhishthira is bewildered, then angrily resolves to stay with them.

scenes.B18C002S01: Yudhishthira says heaven is empty without his brothers and allies, and the gods agree to show him where they are.
scenes.B18C002S02: The messenger leads Yudhishthira along a hellish path until he stops, and Yudhishthira, disgusted, starts to turn back.
scenes.B18C002S03: Pleading voices surround Yudhishthira and each names a dead hero or Draupadi.
scenes.B18C002S04: Yudhishthira wonders what sin could have brought these righteous people to hell, then curses the gods and resolves to stay with them.

shots.B18C002S01H01: Yudhishthira says heaven is empty without his brothers and allies, and asks to see the great warriors who died for him.
shots.B18C002S01H02: The gods tell him that if he longs to be with them, he may go, and they will do as he wishes.
shots.B18C002S01H03: The messenger leads Yudhishthira along a foul, dark road to where his fallen comrades are.
shots.B18C002S01H04: The road is described in detail: boiling rivers, razor-leaved trees, iron jars of boiling oil, and tortured sinners.
shots.B18C002S01H05: Yudhishthira asks how much farther they must go, where his brothers are, and what region this is.
shots.B18C002S02H01: The messenger says this is as far as he may go and offers to take Yudhishthira back if he is tired.
shots.B18C002S02H02: Overcome by the stench, Yudhishthira turns to go back, then hears pleas from all sides to stay a moment longer.
shots.B18C002S02H03: Yudhishthira cries out in pity. The voices sound familiar to him, though he cannot place them.
shots.B18C002S02H04: Yudhishthira asks the voices who they are.
shots.B18C002S02H05: Yudhishthira asks the voices who they are and why they remain in this place.
shots.B18C002S03H01: One voice answers, I am Karna.
shots.B18C002S03H02: Other voices claim the names Bhimasena, Arjuna, Nakula and Sahadeva.
shots.B18C002S03H03: More voices name Dhrishtadyumna, Draupadi and the sons of Draupadi.
shots.B18C002S03H04: The narrator notes that the voices spoke in this way.
shots.B18C002S03H05: Yudhishthira wonders what sin these righteous people could have committed, while Duryodhana prospers, and asks whether he is dreaming.
shots.B18C002S04H01: Yudhishthira grows furious, rebukes the gods and Dharma, and tells the messenger to report back that he will stay with his suffering brothers. The messenger reports to Indra.

B18C003.summary: The gods arrive, and the hellish sights and smells vanish. Indra and Dharma explain that the whole hell scene was an illusion and a test, and that Yudhishthira's time there was linked to his earlier deception of Drona. Yudhishthira bathes in the Ganga, sheds his human body, and is freed of enmity and grief.

scenes.B18C003S01: The gods arrive and the hellish scene disappears. Indra and Dharma explain the hell vision was a test and an illusion, and Dharma praises his son.
scenes.B18C003S02: Yudhishthira bathes in the Ganga, takes a celestial form, and goes on with the gods to the place where the heroes are.

shots.B18C003S01H01: The gods, led by Indra, and Dharma arrive, the darkness lifts, the hellish sights vanish, and a pleasant breeze blows.
shots.B18C003S01H02: Indra welcomes Yudhishthira, says the illusions have ended, and explains that Yudhishthira was shown hell because of his earlier deception of Drona. He says the sinners, including Yudhishthira's brothers and allies, have all been cleansed.
shots.B18C003S01H03: Indra says Karna has gained success, urges Yudhishthira to let go of grief, and invites him to enjoy the heavenly regions he earned, including those won by the Rajasuya sacrifice. He names royal sages who dwell there and points to the Ganga as the way to cleanse his human nature.
shots.B18C003S01H04: Dharma praises his son for devotion, truthfulness and self-control, and says this was the third test, recalling the earlier tests at the lake and in the form of a dog.
shots.B18C003S01H05: Dharma says his brothers did not deserve hell and that the whole affair was an illusion made by Indra. He says Draupadi did not deserve it either, and urges Yudhishthira to bathe in the Ganga.
shots.B18C003S02H01: Yudhishthira bathes in the Ganga, casts off his human body, and is freed of enmity and grief. Surrounded by the gods, he proceeds to the heroes, the Pandavas and Dhartarashtras, who are at peace in their places.

B18C004.summary: Praised by the gods, Yudhishthira goes to where his relatives and allies dwell in heaven. He sees Govinda, Phalguna, Karna, Bhima, the twins, and Draupadi, and Indra explains who each one is and where each now lives. The chapter shows the dead heroes reunited in heaven.

scenes.B18C004S01: Yudhishthira finds his kin and allies in heaven, and Indra explains the identity and place of each one he sees.

shots.B18C004S01H01: Yudhishthira, praised by gods and sages, goes to where the Kuru heroes are. He sees Govinda in his Brahma-form, and Phalguna adoring him, and they greet him with honor.
shots.B18C004S01H02: He sees Karna shining like many suns, Bhima sitting among the Maruts beside the wind god, and the twins Nakula and Sahadeva in the place of the Ashvinis.
shots.B18C004S01H03: He sees Draupadi, wearing lotus garlands and shining with sunlike splendor. Yudhishthira wants to question her, but Indra speaks first, explaining that she was born for Yudhishthira's sake and that the five sons were his and hers.
shots.B18C004S01H04: Indra identifies more of the dead: Dhritarashtra as a Gandharva king, Karna as Yudhishthira's eldest brother, Abhimanyu with Soma, Pandu with Kunti and Madri, Bhishma among the Vasus, and Drona beside Brihaspati. Other kings who fought for Duryodhana now move among the Gandharvas and Yakshas, having earned heaven by their merit.

B18C005.summary: Janamejaya asks how long his heroic ancestors stayed in heaven and whether their place there is lasting. Vaishampayana answers by naming where each great warrior was absorbed after death, and the narrator then closes the whole work with praise of its virtues and of who recites it. The chapter ends the Svargarohana Parva and the frame of the Mahabharata's telling.

scenes.B18C005S01: Janamejaya asks about the fate of the heroes, and Vaishampayana explains where each one went after death, then the snake sacrifice ends and Janamejaya returns home.
scenes.B18C005S02: Sauti describes the work's composer, its purpose, and the merits of reciting or hearing it, including the reason for its name.
scenes.B18C005S03: The narrator recalls Vyasa's verses on the transience of life and the eternity of righteousness, and closes with praise of the work.

shots.B18C005S01H01: Janamejaya asks how long Bhishma, Drona, Dhritarashtra, Karna, Ghatotkaca and many others remained in heaven, and whether their place there is lasting.
shots.B18C005S01H02: Sauti says the Rishi, with Vyasa's permission, begins to answer the king's question.
shots.B18C005S01H03: Vaishampayana says not everyone returns to his own nature when his deeds end, and that Vyasa, who knows the end of every act, taught him this mystery.
shots.B18C005S01H04: A long catalogue follows. Bhishma joins the Vasus, Drona enters Brihaspati, Abhimanyu enters Soma, Karna enters Surya, Yudhishthira joins the god of Righteousness, and Vasudeva enters Narayana. The 16,000 wives of Vasudeva rise to heaven as Apsaras after plunging into the Sarasvati. The fallen warriors become gods or Yakshas, and Duryodhana's side become Rakshasas.
shots.B18C005S01H05: Sauti says Janamejaya was amazed. The priests finish the rites, Astika is glad, Janamejaya gives gifts to the Brahmanas, and he returns to the city named after the elephant.
shots.B18C005S02H01: Sauti says he has told everything that Vaishampayana recited at the snake sacrifice, at Vyasa's command. He describes the composer, Krishna, as a truthful and all-knowing sage, and says the work aims to spread the fame of the Pandavas and other Kshatriyas.
shots.B18C005S02H02: Those who recite or hear the work are promised cleansing of sins, a place in heaven, and food for the ancestors at rites.
shots.B18C005S02H03: The name is explained. The work's topic is the Bharata family, so it is called Bharata, and its great weight makes it Mahabharata. Those who understand it are cleansed and may reach liberation.
shots.B18C005S02H04: The work is said to hold everything found elsewhere. It is called Jaya, and Krishna made a shorter version and a longer one of sixty lakhs of verses, divided among the worlds of the gods, Pitris, Yakshas and humans.
shots.B18C005S02H05: Narada recited it to the gods, Asita-Devala to the Pitris, Suka to the Rakshasas and Yakshas, and Vaishampayana to human beings. Listening with devotion brings fame and cleansing.
shots.B18C005S03H01: Vyasa had his son Suka recite the work along with four verses on life's transience, the fleeting nature of joy and fear, righteousness as the lasting good, and the eternal soul.
shots.B18C005S03H02: Reciting the work at dawn brings reward and high success. The work is compared to the ocean and the Himalayas as a mine of gems, and is praised as nectar and sacred.

B18C006.summary: Janamejaya asks how a learned listener should hear the Bharata, what rites apply, and what rewards follow. Vaishampayana describes the work's scope, the qualities of a good reciter and listener, the heavenly rewards for hearing each portion, and the gifts due at each parva. The chapter closes with praise of the Mahabharata and the note that its eighteen parvas are complete, and it ends with a Project Gutenberg license notice that is not part of the epic.

scenes.B18C006S01: Janamejaya asks about rites, rewards and gifts, and Vaishampayana introduces the work's scope, the merit of listening, and the gifts owed to honored persons and Brahmanas.
scenes.B18C006S02: The manner of reciting is described, and the first four parvas of recitation each bring rewards equal to great sacrifices.
scenes.B18C006S03: The fifth through tenth parvas bring richer heavenly rewards, with cars, Apsaras and time spent with the gods.
scenes.B18C006S04: The listener's heavenly life and the gifts due to the reciter are described, followed by the first feasts to give at the early parvas.
scenes.B18C006S05: The gifts for the parvas from Arani through Karna are listed, mostly food, robes, water pots and weapons.
scenes.B18C006S06: The gifts for the parvas from Shalya through Asramvasika are listed, mostly food and gems.
scenes.B18C006S07: The gifts for the last parvas are listed, followed by worship of the complete book and the final gifts and feasts.
scenes.B18C006S08: The closing praise says the work is sacred and leads to liberation and Vishnu, and the Svargarohanika parva and the whole work are declared complete.
scenes.B18C006S09: Project Gutenberg license notice appended to the file.

shots.B18C006S01H01: Janamejaya asks what rites should be followed in hearing the Bharata, what rewards follow, which deities to worship, which gifts to give at each parva, and what qualities the reciter should have.
shots.B18C006S01H02: Vaishampayana says he will explain briefly. The work contains the births of gods and Rishis and the whole universe, including the Rudras, Adityas, Gandharvas, mountains and seasons.
shots.B18C006S01H03: Hearing the work cleanses even terrible sins. The listener should make offerings to the honored figures and give Brahmanas cattle, gems, maidens, land, cloth, conveyances and other goods, even one's own self.
shots.B18C006S01H04: The listener should hear the work without doubt, with cheer and joy, and give gifts according to his means as he listens.
shots.B18C006S01H05: The listener must be truthful, self-controlled and faithful. The reciter must be pure, learned, white-clad, free of malice and generous.
shots.B18C006S02H01: The reciter should recite calmly, clearly and sweetly, with proper emphasis, and begin with a salute to Narayana, Nara and Sarasvati and the word Jaya.
shots.B18C006S02H02: At the first Parana, gifts to Brahmanas earn the reward of the Agnishtoma sacrifice and a heavenly car with Apsaras in attendance.
shots.B18C006S02H03: At the second Parana, the listener earns the reward of the Atiratra vow and rides a car made of precious gems, receiving high honor in heaven.
shots.B18C006S02H04: At the third Parana, the listener earns the reward of the Dwadasaha vow and lives in heaven for countless years like a god.
shots.B18C006S02H05: At the fourth Parana, the listener earns the reward of the Vajapeya sacrifice.
shots.B18C006S03H01: At the fifth Parana, the fruits are doubled. The listener rides a car like the rising sun and enjoys bliss with Indra for many years.
shots.B18C006S03H02: The sixth Parana doubles the fruits and the seventh triples them, with a car like the Kailasa peak and Apsaras to wait on him.
shots.B18C006S03H03: The eighth Parana brings the reward of the Rajasuya sacrifice. The listener rides a moon-bright car, served by beautiful women, and rests in their laps.
shots.B18C006S03H04: The ninth Parana brings the reward of the Horse-sacrifice. The listener rides a golden-pillared car with Apsaras and Gandharvas around him.
shots.B18C006S03H05: The tenth Parana brings a bell-hung car, crowned and gleaming, from which he roams the heavenly regions.
shots.B18C006S04H01: The listener is honored in heaven for 21,000 years, visiting the regions of the Sun, Moon, Siva and Vishnu. The reciter should be given animals, cars, gold, cloth and perfume, and worshipped as a god.
shots.B18C006S04H02: Gifts should be given to Brahmanas and Kshatriyas after checking their birth, character and devotion. Blessings are said before the reading, and the reciter is first fed honey and frumenty.
shots.B18C006S04H03: During the Astika-parva, Brahmanas are fed fruit, roots, frumenty, honey, clarified butter and sweet rice.
shots.B18C006S04H04: During the Sabha-parva, Brahmanas are fed havisya along with cakes and sweets.
shots.B18C006S04H05: During the Aranyaka-parva, the superior Brahmanas are fed fruit and roots.
shots.B18C006S05H01: During the Arani-parva, water pots and many kinds of fine food, rice and fruit are given to Brahmanas.
shots.B18C006S05H02: During the Virata-parva, robes are given. During the Udyoga-parva, Brahmanas receive perfume, garlands and fine food.
shots.B18C006S05H03: During the Bhishma-parva, cars and conveyances are given, along with pure, well-cooked food.
shots.B18C006S05H04: During the Drona-parva, Brahmanas receive superior food, beds, bows and swords.
shots.B18C006S05H05: During the Karna-parva, the householder feeds Brahmanas the finest pure, well-cooked food with a focused mind.
shots.B18C006S06H01: During the Shalya-parva, sweets, sweet rice, wheat cakes, and nourishing food and drink are given.
shots.B18C006S06H02: During the Gada-parva, Brahmanas are fed food mixed with mudga.
shots.B18C006S06H03: During the Stri-parva, Brahmanas receive gems and precious stones. During the Aishika-parva, ghee-rice comes first, then fine food.
shots.B18C006S06H04: During the Shanti-parva, Brahmanas are fed havisya.
shots.B18C006S06H05: During the Asvamedhika-parva, agreeable food is given. During the Asramvasika-parva, Brahmanas are fed havisya.
shots.B18C006S07H01: During the Mausala-parva, scents and pleasing garlands are given.
shots.B18C006S07H02: During the Mahaprasthanika-parva, similar agreeable presents are given.
shots.B18C006S07H03: During the Svarga-parva, Brahmanas are fed havisya.
shots.B18C006S07H04: When the Harivansa ends, a thousand Brahmanas are fed, each receives a cow with a gold piece, and the poor receive half of that.
shots.B18C006S07H05: When all the parvas are done, the householder gives the reciter a copy of the Mahabharata with gold. The book is worshipped with rites, gifts and feasts for Brahmanas, and the reciter must be learned and clear of voice.
shots.B18C006S08H01: Vaishampayana says he has given the rules as asked, urges the king to follow them with faith, and praises the Bharata as sacred, the highest scripture, and a path to liberation.
shots.B18C006S08H02: The Bharata praises Hari in the Vedas, Ramayana and itself. Listening destroys sin like sunrise dispels darkness. Women seeking children are urged to hear it, and gifts such as a gold-horned cow, ornaments and land are recommended, along with a homa after the reading.
shots.B18C006S08H03: Anyone who listens devotedly is cleansed of every sin, even grave ones, and reaches the realm of Vishnu.
shots.B18C006S08H04: Heading: the end of the Svargarohanika-parva.
shots.B18C006S08H05: Closing line: the Eighteen parvas of the Mahabharata are now complete.
shots.B18C006S09H01: Project Gutenberg license heading. This is editorial boilerplate at the end of the file, not part of the epic.
